page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data needs, while network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect strong single-core compute capabilities alongside middle-tier multi-threaded and memory throughput. The instance achieves a top-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 2695.99, while its multi-core result of 10782.31 and Geekbench scores (1535 single-core and 5877 multi-core) sit comfortably in the middle 50 percent range. Memory subsystems exhibit standard performance on cached operations with 518.66 GB/sec on 16 KB blocks, though uncached large-block read and write speeds drop to 39.27 GB/sec and 18.99 GB/sec respectively. Application-level evaluations show consistent mid-range handling, recording 8.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.57 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its balanced compute and memory distribution, the ecs.g7a.2xlarge represents an efficient deployment target for general enterprise workloads that do not demand extreme uncached memory throughput or local NVMe storage. Primary suitable workloads include web serving, microservices application layers, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build runners, and general backend data processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical AMD EPYC 7T83 cores at 2.55 GHz and 32.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the KVM hypervisor without bundled local storage or GPUs, it utilizes remote network storage and operates on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data demonstrates top-quartile single-core CPU execution alongside balanced middle-tier multi-core, compilation, and web serving capabilities, despite lower throughput on uncached large-block memory operations. The balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio provides predictable, stable performance for general-purpose workloads, including web servers, application middleware, background worker queues, and mid-tier database hosting.
